doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Bass playing, avant-garde and the state of the music
title: Going outside and inside with Monk
summary: Ware says that with Monk they went out as far as they liked and returned on a chord, and he did not know the word avant-garde.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: But then Trane said that you were doing things that would be considered free within the structure, within the confines of the music you were playing in the Monk band.

Yeah, well, that was the point. Monk would get up and we could -- that's what I meant when I said go outside and inside. We knew where we were at. We knew the tunes, structure -- you know, could get back in. But we'd take it out as far as we wanted to take it out.
You know, I used to do that and just see how far I could go.

You know? Monk come back in, boom. We know where he's at. We had one chord and we was right back into the thing. That's so far as avantgarde -- I used to kind of run from them. The cats would say, 'Man, you play avantgarde.' It's like Dave [Higgins] would say, 'Man, you know, you're the first cat to play the avantgarde.' I wondered about that. I said, 'What are you talking about?' I didn't look at it like that. I didn't even know the meaning of the word, 'avantgarde.'
